value.body: A trade finance associate works in the part of a bank that handles payments for exports and imports. Employers are banks and the operations centres that process trade transactions for them. A typical day involves checking documents against letter-of-credit terms, processing bills and remittances, and resolving queries from branches and clients.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Com or BBA; MBA (Finance) for some roles

items.label: Core instruments
items.value: Letters of credit, bank guarantees, export and import bills, foreign remittances

items.label: Rules you work with
items.value: International documentary-credit rules (UCP 600), FEMA and RBI directions

items.label: India's merchandise exports
items.source: Ministry of Commerce and Industry release, 15 Apr 2025 (as reported)

items.label: Total exports, goods and services
items.note: RBI data later put it near US$825 billion (as reported)
items.source: Ministry of Commerce and Industry release, 15 Apr 2025 (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a bank's or banking-operations firm's trade finance team through campus or graduate hiring, often as an operations analyst. Commerce and international-business coursework helps; trade-finance certifications are optional add-ons that some employers value.

value.title: At a glance
items: Much of the entry work is process-driven and can run in shifts aligned to other time zones.
Compliance and accuracy are closely monitored.
Next roles: trade finance specialist, team lead, or a move into relationship management or compliance.
